clue.text: See 7
Letters for Foreign Office? Manuscript for groups of supporters

parts.note: the Foreign Office is abbreviated FO, which spelt out as letters is F and O

explanation.surface: A query about the abbreviation for a government department, then a document for fan clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Letters for Foreign Office' as the phrase 'F and O', spelt in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Fan communities collectively are bodies of devoted followers, the plural of a word for a fan base.

clue.text: Called in foxhunting, daughter following you, almost, with "a son of God"?

indicators.note: following means the daughter's letter comes after the other pieces
almost means the last letter of the word you is left off

parts.note: David Icke, the conspiracy theorist, notoriously claimed to be a son of God
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A hunting cry, with a nod to a man proclaiming divine parentage, as in a Life of Brian scene.
explanation.walkthrough: YOICKS is a traditional hunting cry to urge on hounds; the verb form is formed from it. David Icke is a British former sportscaster who in 1991 claimed to be a son of God.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting the traditional huntsman's halloo to hounds is what the verb means, in the past tense.

clue.text: 1930s documentary — decapitating searcher for Holy Grail with his armour?

indicators.note: decapitating removes the head, so the first letter of the searcher is dropped

parts.note: the knights of Arthurian legend went questing for the Holy Grail
mail is the chain armour a knight wears

explanation.surface: A film reference wrapped in a gory image of a beheaded Grail knight in his armour.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1936 GPO film set to Auden's poem is the documentary; Holy Grail also nods to the Python film.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the famous 1936 British Post Office film about the postal train.

clue.text: Works on theme setting on machine

definitions.meaning: a series of musical or literary pieces linked by subject, such as Wagner's Ring
a programme on a washing machine, such as a spin or rinse

explanation.surface: Someone operating a machine and choosing a setting for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A connected sequence of artworks and a washer programme are both called by this word.

clue.text: More prepared, close to Kate Adie in posh car

indicators.note: in means the reporter's pieces sit inside the car's letters

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the archetypal posh car

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of Kate is taken

parts.note: Kate Adie is a well-known BBC war correspondent

explanation.surface: The BBC reporter Kate Adie getting ready in a luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to Kate' gives only E; Adie supplies the rest of the inserted run.
explanation.definitionFit: Better prepared simply means more ready, the comparative of the adjective.

clue.text: Removes ties for Ferry, perhaps onus initially on Roxy Music reform

indicators.note: to reform is to shape anew, so the gathered letters are rearranged
initially takes the opening letter of each of the words on, Roxy and Music

explanation.surface: Bryan Ferry is freed of obligations by a Roxy Music reunion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives ORM from On Roxy Music; 'reform' shuffles ONUS plus ORM. Ferry looks like Bryan Ferry, Roxy Music's singer, but means a boat leaving its moorings.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting off the ropes that hold a boat at the quay frees it from its ties.

clue.text: Rewriting shortly, comics typing funny show

indicators.note: rewriting a text recasts it, so the four following words are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A note on hastily redrafting comedians' scripts for an amusing programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rewriting' turns SHORTLY COMICS TYPING FUNNY, all twenty-four letters, into the full title of the famous BBC comedy series of 1969-74.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the title of a celebrated television comedy programme, so a show by name.

clue.text: Beastly noises from boxing promoter, who doesn't open boxing institute

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the institute's letter is put inside
not opening means the promoter's first letter is lost

parts.note: Don King is the famous American boxing promoter

explanation.surface: Complaints about a boxing promoter who won't open his gym.
explanation.walkthrough: Don King loses his D, and 'boxing' then puts I into ONKING.
explanation.definitionFit: The grunting sounds pigs make are noises from beasts, hence beastly in a literal sense.

clue.text: Couple of blokes and old pedlar

parts.note: a chap is a bloke, giving the first of the pair
a man is a bloke too, giving the second of the pair

explanation.surface: Two men and an elderly hawker.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical term for an itinerant dealer who hawked goods door to door.

clue.text: I criss-cross with salon's manicure equipment

indicators.note: cross here means crossed over or jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word salon's taken with its S as written

explanation.surface: A beauty-salon worker getting cross with the shop's tools.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'criss-cross' does two separate things: its first half is part of the anagram fodder, and its second half, 'cross', is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Small curved-bladed cutters for trimming fingernails are standard manicurist's kit.

clue.text: Loose filling of milk tooth — drill here?

indicators.note: loose means set free, so the extracted letters are scrambled
the filling is the inside, the letters left once the outer two are gone

explanation.surface: A dentist with a wobbly baby tooth needing a filling and drilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling of' takes ILKTOOT from MILK TOOTH; 'Loose' rearranges it. Drill looks like dentistry but is the tool kept in the box.
explanation.definitionFit: A box of tools is where a power drill would be kept, a definition by example.

clue.text: Record one German working with current Greek tragedy

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one
on means working, as a machine that is on
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A recording of a German at work on a Greek tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a lost ancient play about the sons of the Seven against Thebes.

clue.text: Sat and put forward

definitions.meaning: modelled for an artist or photographer, held still
proposed, as a question set before a meeting

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both modelling for a portrait and raising a question for discussion.

clue.text: Disturbing means taking in spoon-bender's abnormal enlargements

indicators.note: taking in means swallowing, so the psychic's letters go inside
disturbing means unsettling, so the letters of means are rearranged

parts.note: Uri Geller is famous for bending spoons; with the possessive this gives Uri's

explanation.surface: Upsetting methods that include a psychic's distorted spoons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbing' rearranges the letters of 'means' into ANEMS, and 'taking in' puts the psychic's name inside it. Uri Geller is the famous spoon-bender.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term for balloon-like swellings in blood vessel walls, a kind of abnormal dilation.

clue.text: Fine Cleese, essentially taking 10 minutes to act around Q's successor

indicators.note: taking means the middle letters take in the numeral
essentially picks the essence, the central letters of the comedian's name

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

indicators.note: around means the verb's letters go round the next letter

parts.note: to play is to act a part
R follows Q in the alphabet

explanation.surface: John Cleese taking ten minutes to act around the Bond gadget-master's replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleese also played R, Q's successor, in the Bond films, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Exemplary conduct is admirable and excellent, which is what fine means here.

clue.text: Tiny bits of mosaic ideal — less ethical having taken piece back

indicators.note: back means the letters taken are read in reverse
a piece is taken from the run of words, so the letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: Someone who has stolen a piece from an ideal mosaic and is less ethical for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having taken piece' lifts EALLESSET from 'idEAL LESS EThical', and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The small square tiles that make up a mosaic, plural of the Latin tile word.

clue.text: Containing tin, like recycled tin cans?

indicators.note: recycled means reprocessed into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemist describing tin cans sent for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost &lit: recycled tin cans literally contain tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry adjective for compounds of tin in its higher valency, from Latin stannum.

clue.text: Material that's stimulating damaged ear — outside of the ear

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters go around the adjective
damaged means broken, so the letters of ear are rearranged

parts.note: otic is the medical adjective meaning of the ear

explanation.surface: A doctor treating an ear damaged on its outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns EAR into ERA, which goes 'outside' OTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexually arousing writing or art is literature meant to excite, hence stimulating.

clue.text: Visitor to Mecca Bingo's second after leaders of house announced joint jackpot

indicators.note: after means the bingo letter follows the initials
leaders are the front runners, the first letters of the four words
second picks the second letter of Bingo

explanation.surface: A bingo caller announcing a shared jackpot at a Mecca Bingo hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Mecca Bingo is a British chain of bingo halls, misdirecting from the holy city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca is given this title.

clue.text: Finish Green — Cluedo's final turn after half of lead piping's seen outside

indicators.note: seen outside means the temperature word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: piping hot means very hot

indicators.note: after means the Cluedo letter and the turn follow the half
half of takes the first two of the four letters of lead
final takes the last letter of Cluedo

parts.note: a U-turn, so U stands for turn

explanation.surface: A Cluedo game: the Reverend Green, lead piping and a final turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted letters go between the second and third letters of the outer word. Green means the golf green, not the Cluedo suspect; Cluedo is a murder-mystery board game.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to sink the ball into the cup and so complete play on the green.

clue.text: Hard to keep up with Neighbours?

definitions.text: Hard to keep up with Neighbours?

parts.words: Hard to keep up with Neighbours?
parts.note: keeping up with the family next door is the idiom for status rivalry; Neighbours is also an Australian soap

explanation.surface: Struggling to follow the plot of the soap opera Neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom keeping up with these names your neighbours whose lifestyle you try to match.

clue.text: Having continuous luck playing craps?

definitions.meaning: literally engaged in throwing dice in the game of craps

explanation.surface: A gambler on a winning streak at the dice table.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having a run of success, and literally fits throwing dice.

clue.text: Insubstantial Daybreak

definitions.meaning: first ..., as in first ... of dawn

explanation.definitionFit: The word means weighing little and also the dawn's illumination.

clue.text: Heather cutting father's fences

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the shrub's letters go inside

parts.note: pa is father, and pa's gives the possessive S
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: Trimming the heather around Dad's fences.
explanation.definitionFit: Fences made of pointed stakes, so a word for fencing by its material.

clue.text: Remitting second resolution

parts.note: an ending resolves a story

explanation.surface: Paying money for a second resolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Remitting money means dispatching it, a synonym for posting it.

clue.text: Viagra? Run out? A drug taker to swallow it

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the cricket letters go into the pieces

parts.note: a user is someone who takes drugs
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: Someone who has run out of Viagra asks a drug-taker to swallow some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to 'Run out' as the thing swallowed. Viagra is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that stimulates arousal is something that excites, an example of the type.

clue.text: They wanted reds out of my architects' design

indicators.note: design means plan or arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Communists expelled from the plans of my architects.
explanation.walkthrough: Reds are communists, purged in 1950s America by Senator Joseph McCarthy's supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of Senator McCarthy's anti-communist purges in 1950s America sought to remove communists.
